newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS - VA Tech posts robust '96 results.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - VA Tech posts robust '96 results.

text.p: Austrian engineering group VA Technologie VAT.VI on Wednesday lived up to its promise of posting double-digit growth in most key earnings in 1996 and vowed it would generate more good news in the current year.

"We'll see double-digit growth again in all key earnings," chief executive Othmar Puehringer told reporters at its annual conference, adding the group would pay close attention to globalisation, technological development and group integration.

Group pretax profit, turnover, and new orders and backlog all showed a substantial increase on the previous year but net profit -- as the company cautioned at the interim period -- was pressured by an increased tax burden.

"Net profit was influenced by a temporarily higher company taxation (due to the suspended use of tax loss carry forwards for 1996 and 1997) as well as by the absence of extraordinary income in 1996," VA Tech said earlier in a statement.

Pretax profit jumped 32 percent to 1.672 billion schillings ($138 million), sales climbed 29 percent to 33.537 billion and order intake rose 26 percent to 44.576 billion, while net profit gained just five percent to 1.404 billion schillings.
Investors welcomed the better-than-expected earnings and confident forecast and duly snapped up the stock, driving it 40 schillings, or 2.35 percent, higher to 1,740 by 0938 GMT.

"The results were pretty amazing. They delivered on their promise of double-digit growth -- and now they say there's more to come," said analyst Alfred Reisenberger of IMI Sigeco in London, adding he maintains his buy recommendation on VA Tech.
The group has shown consistent earnings growth over the past years, with earnings per share (EPS) rising to 84 schillings in 1996 from 56 in 1993.
Based on forecasts compiled by Edinburgh Financial Publishing, a consensus of nine analysts sees EPS growing to 89 schillings this year, with the highest estimate pegged at 92 schillings.

Order backlog again reached a new record at 80.4 billion schillings, up 21 percent from 1995. The company attributed this to its successful risk management, whereby it spreads the sizes of projects so that the group is not dependent on a few major projects.

Indeed, middle-sized projects with a value from 100 million to one billion schillings accounted for approximately 50 percent of the order backlog value, while only 26 percent came from major projects with a value of more than one billion schillings.
The group's order intake, which rose 26 percent, was boosted by the acquisition of Germany's Fuchs Systemtechnik and by the environmental engineering area of Sulzer Chemtech, VA Tech said.

Puehringer attributed last year's strong earnings to the group becoming global market leader in metallurgical plant building and systems supplier for individual and integrated plants, where the order intake surged 60 percent to 15.2 billion schillings.

VA Tech continued its globalisation drive last year. In addition to acquisitions in Germany, Switzerland and Croatia, new international units were established in Brazil and Great Britain as well as joint ventures in Saudi Arabia and India.
VA Tech now has 200 units worldwide. ($ = 12.15 Austrian Schillings)
